rows.title: Lamont hopes cap will keep lawmakers’ hands off $2.5B reserve
rows.standfirst: Connecticut is sitting on a multi-billion-dollar reserve but lawmakers will have to get around the spending cap – and the governor – if they want to tap it.

rows.title: Lamont’s bond presentation could put tolls proposal at risk
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont must decide how much detail about his latest bonding proposal to release to legislators Wednesday, including any proposals that might entice legislators to support his trucks-only tolling plan.

rows.title: Lamont to propose millions for affordable housing construction
rows.standfirst: The governor is planning a sizable investment in affordable housing, but said he is not prepared to submit legislation tackling the state’s high housing costs.

rows.title: Lamont’s new budget takes aim at vaping, debt-free college program
rows.standfirst: There are no major tax hikes in Gov. Ned Lamont’s budget proposal, but it does include a ban on flavored vaping liquids and place restrictions on the debt-free college program.

rows.title: Lamont keeps state spending lean to build reserves against next recession
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont proposed a lean $22.3 billion budget Wednesday that would push Connecticut’s emergency reserves close to $3 billion while keeping taxes largely flat.

rows.title: Lamont eases up on debt diet to win support for truck tolls
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont added an average of $442 million to his two-year bonding proposal — about 20% more than he insisted Connecticut could afford when he took office 13 months ago.

rows.title: Lamont proposes $45M for development authority pushed by tolls ally
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont has proposed borrowing $45 million to launch a transit-oriented development authority that still lacks an oversight board and that he and legislators effectively opted not to fund eight months ago.

rows.title: Fiscal cure sought for UConn Health
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont’s administration is questioning whether the state can afford to continue subsidizing the public teaching hospital.

rows.title: Lamont unveils New London harbor deal as quasi-public debate heats up
rows.standfirst: While the governor celebrated a deal to develop New London harbor and an offshore wind center, the partisan battle over Connecticut’s quasi-publics intensified.

rows.title: Salary battle prompts new questions about privacy rules for education partnership
rows.standfirst: A plan to pay the head of CT’s new education partnership more than $300,000 has prompted renewed questions about the program’s exemption from FOI laws.

rows.title: Progressive Dems renew push for tax reform, legalized cannabis
rows.standfirst: Liberal democrats in the House of Representatives will renew their push this year for a more progressive tax system and legalized cannabis use while also pressing for new labor rules regarding worker schedules and an end to solitary confinement.

rows.title: Pew: CT leads most states in ensuring good return on business incentives
rows.standfirst: Between grants, low-interest loans and tax breaks, Connecticut provides hundreds of millions of dollars annually in incentives to help businesses survive — and sometimes to expand — in a high-cost state. And while these incentives remain a perpetual source of debate, a national think-tank says Connecticut at least does better than most other states at ensuring it gets a good return on its investments.

rows.title: Lamont pledges to release stalled town aid, regardless of whether tolls are approved
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont pledged Wednesday to support borrowing for overdue municipal aid — even if legislators reject his transportation initiative and the truck tolls that would come with it.

rows.title: Lamont keeps pledge, begins release of stalled municipal aid
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont kept his pledge to Connecticut municipalities Friday, beginning the process of releasing $150 million in municipal aid stalled since last summer by the debate over tolls.

rows.title: With CT tolls debate on ice, fiscal issues loom large
rows.standfirst: Connecticut’s tolls debate may be over for now, but that lull only means Gov. Ned Lamont and legislators now must resolve a daunting list of fiscal challenges left in its wake.

rows.title: Legislators who opposed tolls want transit spending in their districts
rows.standfirst: Lawmakers who helped block Gov. Ned Lamont’s plan to increase funding want the state to invest millions on transit improvements in their districts.

rows.title: Democrats: GOP has a healthy appetite for borrowing too
rows.standfirst: Republican leaders may be on the governor’s “debt diet,” but rank-and-file GOP lawmakers are bypassing the proverbial salad bar.

rows.title: Town aid stranded by tolls debate isn’t out of political limbo yet
rows.standfirst: Connecticut’s tolls debate is over, yet millions of dollars in town aid remains in political limbo.
